cohort: The cohort consisted of First Nations pregnancies in the province of Alberta, Canada, between the years 2000 and 2009.
finding: First Nations ethnicity was a significant independent predictor of high birth weight, very high birth weight, and very low birth weight, and while these adverse birth weight prevalences remain higher than the general population, they are not increasing.
birth_weight: High birth weight (> 4000g), very high birth weight (> 4500g), low birth weight (< 2500g), very low birth weight (< 1500g)
